nodes.summary: For every odd natural number $q > 3$ there is exactly one odd natural number $x$ such that $\{4, x\}$ is an N-position and $\{4, x, q\}$ is a P-position.
nodes.title: Odd numbers above 3 have a unique odd partner after 4

nodes.summary: For every odd natural number $x \ge 5$ there is exactly one legal move $q$ of the position $\{4, x\}$ such that $\{4, x, q\}$ is a P-position, and every legal move $q$ of $\{4, x\}$ with $\{4, x, q\}$ a P-position satisfies $q \equiv x - 2 \pmod 4$.
nodes.title: Sicherman's claim on replies to 4 and an odd number

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a position of Sylver Coinage whose set of legal moves $L(M)$ has a greatest element $F$. Then $F$ is an end of $M$.
nodes.title: The largest legal move is an end

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a position of Sylver Coinage with set of legal moves $L(M)$. A natural number $x$ is an end of $M$ if $x \in L(M)$ and every $y \in L(M)$ with $y \ne x$ is still a legal move of the position $M \cup \{x\}$; that is, naming $x$ eliminates no other legal move.
nodes.title: Ends of a Sylver Coinage position

nodes.summary: Let $x \ge 5$ be an odd natural number. For every even legal move $b$ of the position $\{4, x\}$, the position $\{4, x, b\}$ is an N-position.
nodes.title: Even replies to 4 and an odd number at least 5 lose

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a position of Sylver Coinage whose set of legal moves $L(M)$ has a greatest element $F$ with $F > 1$. If every end of $M$ equals $F$ (that is, $M$ is an ender), then $M$ is an N-position.
nodes.title: Enders with largest legal move above 1 are N-positions

nodes.summary: The position $\{2\}$ of Sylver Coinage is an N-position: the player to move wins by naming $3$, which leaves the P-position $\{2, 3\}$.
nodes.title: Opening with 2 loses

nodes.summary: A position $M$ of Sylver Coinage is an N-position (the player to move wins) when either $1 \in M$, so that the previous player named $1$ and lost, or some legal move $q$ of $M$ leads to a P-position $M \cup \{q\}$. N-positions and P-positions are defined together inductively by these rules.
nodes.title: N-positions of Sylver Coinage

nodes.summary: Let $x > 1$ be a natural number. If $x \equiv 1 \pmod 4$, then $\{4, x, x + 2, 6\}$ is a P-position; if $x \equiv 7 \pmod 8$, then $\{4, x, x + 2, 10\}$ is a P-position; if $x \equiv 5 \pmod 8$, then $\{4, x, x + 6, 10\}$ is a P-position; and if $x \equiv 1 \pmod 8$, then $\{4, x, x + 6, 14\}$ is a P-position.
nodes.title: Four-element P-positions containing 4

nodes.summary: For every prime $p > 3$, the position $\{p\}$ of Sylver Coinage is a P-position: a first player who opens with $p$ wins.
nodes.title: Hutchings' theorem

nodes.summary: In Sylver Coinage, the position $\{2, 3\}$ is a P-position: its only legal move is $1$.
nodes.title: The position $\{2, 3\}$ is a P-position

nodes.summary: A set $M$ of natural numbers is a P-position of Sylver Coinage when $1 \notin M$ and, for every legal move $q$ of $M$, the position $M \cup \{q\}$ is an N-position. P-positions and N-positions are defined together, as a mutual inductive definition. In particular a position whose only legal move is $1$ is a P-position (the player to move must name $1$ and loses).
nodes.title: P-positions of Sylver Coinage

nodes.title: Pseudo-symmetric semigroups of multiplicity 4 and embedding dimension 3

nodes.summary: Let $a$, $b$ and $F$ be natural numbers and let $S = \langle a, b \rangle$ be the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $a$ and $b$. If $F \notin S$ and every natural number $n > F$ lies in $S$ (so $F$ is the Frobenius number of $S$), then $x \in S \iff F - x \notin S$ for every natural number $x \le F$.
nodes.title: Two-generated numerical semigroups are symmetric

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a set of natural numbers whose set of legal moves $L(M)$ has a greatest element $F > 1$, and suppose that $F$ is the only end of $M$ (so $M$ is an ender). Then for every legal move $x$ of $M$ with $x < F$, the number $F$ is not a legal move of $M \cup \{x\}$.
nodes.title: In an ender, every smaller move eliminates the largest legal move

nodes.summary: Let $q$ and $x$ be odd natural numbers with $7 < q < x$ such that $\{4, x\}$ is an N-position and $\{4, x, q\}$ is a P-position of Sylver Coinage. Then $2q < x < 3q$.
nodes.title: Conway's bounds for 4-pairs

nodes.summary: Let $q > 3$ be an odd natural number. Then $\{4, q\}$ is an N-position of Sylver Coinage, and there is a unique odd natural number $x_q$ such that $\{4, x_q\}$ is an N-position and $\{4, q, x_q\}$ is a P-position.
nodes.title: Unique odd partner after 4

nodes.summary: For a set $M$ of natural numbers (a position of Sylver Coinage), the set $L(M)$ of legal moves consists of the natural numbers that are not finite sums of elements of $M$, repetitions allowed, i.e. the natural numbers outside the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $M$. Since $0$ is the empty sum, every legal move is positive.
nodes.title: Legal moves in Sylver Coinage

nodes.summary: Let $M$ be a finite set of natural numbers whose set of legal moves $L(M)$ is finite, and suppose that removing any element changes the legal moves: $L(M \setminus \{a\}) \ne L(M)$ for every $a \in M$. Let $S$ be the additive submonoid of $\mathbb{N}$ generated by $M$. Then $M$ is the set of nonzero elements $s \in S$ such that whenever $s = a + b$ with $a, b \in S$, one of $a$ and $b$ is $0$; that is, $M$ is the…
nodes.title: A canonical position is the minimal generating set of its semigroup

nodes.summary: For every set $M$ of natural numbers, $0$ is not a legal move of the Sylver Coinage position $M$.
nodes.title: Zero is never a legal move

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
